parts.zh: M: 你做市场调研顾问有多久了？
W: 嗯，我大学毕业后就马上开始做了
M: 你学的是市场调研吗？
W: 是的，这确实帮助我进入了这个行业
M: 那你对什么感兴趣？
W: 嗯，目前我专门从事定量广告研究
M: 你说的临时项目具体是什么意思？
W: 基本上就是公司需要迅速得到关于消费者习惯的问题答案时开展的项目
W: 两种我都喜欢，事实上
M: 你能简单解释一下你和新客户合作时会经历什么流程吗？

items.stem: What position does the woman hold in the company?

choices.text: Project organizer.
choices.zh: 项目组织者。

choices.text: Public relations officer.
choices.zh: 公共关系专员。

choices.text: Marketing manager.
choices.zh: 营销经理。

choices.text: Market research consultant.
choices.zh: 市场研究顾问。

items.stem: What does the woman specialize in at the moment?

choices.text: Quantitative advertising research.
choices.zh: 定量广告研究。

choices.text: Questionnaire design.
choices.zh: 问卷设计。

choices.text: Research methodology.
choices.zh: 研究方法论。

choices.text: Interviewer training.
choices.zh: 访谈员培训。

items.stem: What does the woman say about trackers?

choices.text: They are intensive studies of people's spending habits.
choices.zh: 它们是对人们消费习惯的深入研究。

choices.text: They examine relations between producers and customers.
choices.zh: 它们考察生产者与消费者之间的关系。

choices.text: They look for new and effective ways to promote products.
choices.zh: 它们寻找推广产品的新颖有效的方式。

choices.text: They study trends or customer satisfaction over a long period.
choices.zh: 它们长期研究趋势或客户满意度。

items.stem: What does the woman dislike about her job?

choices.text: The lack of promotion opportunity.
choices.zh: 缺乏晋升机会。

choices.text: Checking charts and tables.
choices.zh: 检查图表。

choices.text: Designing questionnaires.
choices.zh: 设计问卷。

choices.text: The persistent intensity.
choices.zh: 持续的高强度。

items.stem: What does the woman want Frederick to talk about?

choices.text: His view on Canadian universities.
choices.zh: 他对加拿大大学的看法。

choices.text: His understanding of higher education.
choices.zh: 他对高等教育的理解。

choices.text: His suggestions for improvements in higher education.
choices.zh: 他对改进高等教育的建议。

choices.text: His complaint about bureaucracy in American universities.
choices.zh: 他对美国大学官僚主义的抱怨。

items.stem: What does the man say about the curriculum in Canadian universities?

choices.text: It is well designed.
choices.zh: 设计得很好。

choices.text: It is rather inflexible.
choices.zh: 相当不灵活。

choices.text: It varies among universities.
choices.zh: 各大学之间有所不同。

choices.text: It has undergone great changes.
choices.zh: 已经历了巨大变化。

items.stem: On what point do the speakers agree?

choices.text: The United States and Canada can learn from each other.
choices.zh: 美国和加拿大可以相互学习。

choices.text: Public universities are often superior to private universities.
choices.zh: 公立大学通常优于私立大学。

choices.text: Everyone should be given equal access to higher education.
choices.zh: 每个人都应该获得平等的高等教育机会。

choices.text: Private schools work more efficiently than public institutions.
choices.zh: 私立学校比公立机构运作效率更高。

items.stem: What point does the man make at the end of the conversation?

choices.text: University systems vary from country to country.
choices.zh: 大学体系因国家而异。

choices.text: Efficiency is essential to university management.
choices.zh: 效率对大学管理至关重要。

choices.text: It is hard to say which is better, a public university or a private one.
choices.zh: 很难说公立大学和私立大学哪个更好。

choices.text: Many private universities in the U.S. are actually large bureaucracies.
choices.zh: 美国许多私立大学实际上是大型官僚机构。

items.stem: What is the International Labor Organization's report mainly about?

choices.text: Government's role in resolving an economic crisis.
choices.zh: 政府在解决经济危机中的作用。

choices.text: The worsening real wage situation around the world.
choices.zh: 全球实际工资状况的恶化。

choices.text: Indications of economic recovery in the United States.
choices.zh: 美国经济复苏的迹象。

choices.text: The impact of the current economic crisis on people's life.
choices.zh: 当前经济危机对人们生活的影响。

items.stem: According to an International Labor Organization's specialist, how will employers feel if there are more people looking for jobs?

choices.text: They will feel less pressure to raise employees' wages.
choices.zh: 他们提高员工工资的压力会减小。

choices.text: They will feel free to choose the most suitable employees.
choices.zh: 他们可以自由选择最合适的员工。

choices.text: They will feel inclined to expand their business operations.
choices.zh: 他们会倾向于扩大业务运营。

choices.text: They will feel more confident in competing with their rivals.
choices.zh: 他们在与竞争对手竞争时会更有信心。

items.stem: What does the speaker mean by the Work Sharing scheme?

choices.text: Employees and companies cooperate to pull through the economic crisis.
choices.zh: 员工和公司合作共渡经济危机。

choices.text: Government and companies join hands to create jobs for the unemployed.
choices.zh: 政府和公司携手为失业者创造就业机会。

choices.text: Employees work shorter hours to avoid layoffs.
choices.zh: 员工缩短工作时间以避免裁员。

choices.text: Team work will be encouraged in companies.
choices.zh: 公司将鼓励团队合作。

items.stem: What question is frequently put to the speaker?

choices.text: Whether memory supplements work.
choices.zh: 记忆补充剂是否有效。

choices.text: Whether herbal medicine works wonders.
choices.zh: 草药是否有神奇功效。

choices.text: Whether exercise enhances one's memory.
choices.zh: 运动是否能增强记忆力。

choices.text: Whether a magic memory promises success.
choices.zh: 神奇的记忆力是否能带来成功。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about most memory supplements?

choices.text: They help the elderly more than the young.
choices.zh: 它们对老年人比对年轻人更有帮助。

choices.text: They are beneficial in one way or another.
choices.zh: 它们在某种程度上是有益的。

choices.text: They generally do not have side effects.
choices.zh: 它们通常没有副作用。

choices.text: They are not based on real science.
choices.zh: 它们不是基于真正的科学。

items.stem: What do we learn about memory supplements in eastern cultures?

choices.text: They are available at most country fairs.
choices.zh: 它们在大多数乡村集市上都能买到。

choices.text: They are taken in relatively high dosage.
choices.zh: 它们的服用剂量相对较高。

choices.text: They are collected or grown by farmers.
choices.zh: 它们由农民采集或种植。

choices.text: They are prescribed by trained practitioners.
choices.zh: 它们由受过训练的从业者开具处方。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about memory supplements at the end?

choices.text: They have often proved to be as helpful as doing mental exercise.
choices.zh: 它们经常被证明与做脑力锻炼一样有帮助。

choices.text: Taking them with other medications might entail unnecessary risks.
choices.zh: 将它们与其他药物一起服用可能带来不必要的风险。

choices.text: Their effect lasts only a short time.
choices.zh: 它们的效果只能持续很短时间。

choices.text: Many have benefited from them.
choices.zh: 许多人从中受益。

items.stem: What is the talk mainly about?

choices.text: How catastrophic natural disasters turn out to be to developing nations.
choices.zh: 灾难性自然灾害对发展中国家造成多么严重的后果。

choices.text: How the World Meteorological Organization studies natural disasters.
choices.zh: 世界气象组织如何研究自然灾害。

choices.text: How powerless humans appear to be in face of natural disasters.
choices.zh: 人类在自然灾害面前显得多么无能为力。

choices.text: How the negative impacts of natural disasters can be reduced.
choices.zh: 如何减少自然灾害的负面影响。

items.stem: How can we stop extreme events from turning into disasters?

choices.text: By training rescue teams for emergencies.
choices.zh: 通过培训应急救援队伍。

choices.text: By taking steps to prepare people for them.
choices.zh: 通过采取措施让人们为极端事件做好准备。

choices.text: By changing people's views of nature.
choices.zh: 通过改变人们对自然的看法。

choices.text: By relocating people to safer places.
choices.zh: 通过将人们迁移到更安全的地方。

items.stem: What does the example of Cuba serve to show?

choices.text: How preventive action can reduce the loss of life.
choices.zh: 预防性行动如何能够减少生命损失。

choices.text: How courageous Cubans are in face of disasters.
choices.zh: 古巴人在灾难面前多么勇敢。

choices.text: How Cubans suffer from tropical storms.
choices.zh: 古巴人如何遭受热带风暴的侵袭。

choices.text: How destructive tropical storms can be.
choices.zh: 热带风暴的破坏性有多大。

items.stem: What does President Obama hope the banks will do?

choices.text: Pay back their loans to the American government.
choices.zh: 偿还它们欠美国政府的贷款。

choices.text: Provide loans to those in severe financial difficulty.
choices.zh: 向那些处于严重财务困境中的人提供贷款。

choices.text: Contribute more to the goal of a wider recovery.
choices.zh: 为实现更广泛的经济复苏目标作出更多贡献。

choices.text: Speed up their recovery from the housing bubble.
choices.zh: 加快它们从房地产泡沫中的复苏。

items.stem: What is Martin Neil Baily's prediction about the financial situation in the future?

choices.text: Some banks may have to merge with others.
choices.zh: 一些银行可能不得不与其他银行合并。

choices.text: Many smaller regional banks are going to fail.
choices.zh: 许多规模较小的地区性银行将会倒闭。

choices.text: It will be hard for banks to provide more loans.
choices.zh: 银行将难以提供更多贷款。

choices.text: Many banks will have to lay off some employees.
choices.zh: 许多银行将不得不裁减一些员工。

items.stem: What does U.S. Bancorp chief Richard Davis say about its future operation?

choices.text: It will work closely with the government.
choices.zh: 它将与政府密切合作。

choices.text: It will endeavor to write off bad loans.
choices.zh: 它将努力核销不良贷款。

choices.text: It will try to lower the interest rate.
choices.zh: 它将努力降低利率。

choices.text: It will try to provide more loans.
choices.zh: 它将努力提供更多贷款。

items.stem: What does Martin Neil Baily think of a second stimulus to the economy?

choices.text: It won't help the American economy to turn around.
choices.zh: 它不会帮助美国经济扭转局面。

choices.text: It won't do any good to the major commercial banks.
choices.zh: 它对主要商业银行不会有任何好处。

choices.text: It will win the approval of the Obama administration.
choices.zh: 它将赢得奥巴马政府的批准。

choices.text: It will be necessary if the economy starts to shrink again.
choices.zh: 如果经济再次开始萎缩,它将是必要的。

items.stem: According to the speaker, what might be a symptom of cognitive decline in older adults?

choices.text: Being unable to learn new things.
choices.zh: 无法学习新事物。

choices.text: Being rather slow to make changes.
choices.zh: 做出改变相当缓慢。

choices.text: Losing temper more and more often.
choices.zh: 越来越频繁地发脾气。

choices.text: Losing the ability to get on with others.
choices.zh: 失去与他人相处的能力。

items.stem: According to James Burke, what does seem to help reduce cognitive decline?

choices.text: Cognitive stimulation.
choices.zh: 认知刺激。

choices.text: Community activity.
choices.zh: 社区活动。

choices.text: Balanced diet.
choices.zh: 均衡饮食。

choices.text: Fresh air.
choices.zh: 新鲜空气。

items.stem: What did James Burke recommend to reduce the incidence of cognitive decline?

choices.text: Ignoring the signs and symptoms of aging.
choices.zh: 忽视衰老的迹象和症状。

choices.text: Adopting an optimistic attitude towards life.
choices.zh: 对生活采取乐观态度。

choices.text: Endeavoring to give up unhealthy lifestyles.
choices.zh: 努力放弃不健康的生活方式。

choices.text: Seeking advice from doctors from time to time.
choices.zh: 不时向医生寻求建议。
